description: Hello! My name is Konouz and I'm forming a super duper awesome team to help create something impactful! I am deeply passionate about space, astronomy, and creating cool software using code. In this challenge we will be tackling the very difficult but rewarding problem of mapping a huge space dataset into comprehensible visualizations via a web interface to make it easier for regular folks and also scientists to make sense of new data. If you like winning, learning, and having fun, join my team!
summary:
Felicia is an educational space gaming hub with games ranging from easy difficulty to harder difficulty, along with games focusing on specific subsystems of an entire space mission. There are a total of 5 games that range from building a rocket to CO-OP 4-player rocket system management with detailed mission milestone engagement and CO-OP space mission management.

The games allow players to build rockets within constraint and specific parameter requirements, fly into orbit, and land on Mars or the moon for further scientific data collection. For the terrain data or estimation of slopes and positions, we used data from the Reconnaissance Orbiter data for the Apollo 15 region and NASA/JPL and USGS
details:
Felecia: The Space Engineering Adventure is an educational spaceflight and mission-design game built as part of the Orbital Frontier project. Players choose a mission, design a spacecraft, and guide it from launch toward an orbital or lunar objective. In the main Voyager campaign, players balance a rocket’s cost, mass, thrust, fuel, power, and scientific equipment; launch and stage it; navigate the flight; and, on lunar missions, land and explore the surface. The rover expedition adds science sites to visit and data to collect. Different difficulty levels offer guided play for newcomers as well as more manual, demanding controls.

The game makes the connections between engineering decisions visible. Changing a component can affect whether a spacecraft meets its budget, has enough thrust or delta-v, or can supply its instruments with power. Players can experiment, see the consequences, and receive mission feedback. The intended benefit is to make space-science and aerospace concepts more approachable while encouraging systems thinking, planning, and problem-solving. The project aims to spark interest in STEM and space exploration; it is an educational simulation, not a tool for real mission planning.

The project was developed primarily with Unity 6.0.62f1 and C#, using the Universal Render Pipeline. The current itch.io version is a Unity WebGL build, packaged to run in a browser using Unity’s HTML and JavaScript loader and WebAssembly player. The wider repository also contains separate browser technology, including .NET 8, C#, WebAssembly, Three.js, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, and an ASP.NET Core crew-host component; those are distinct from this Unity WebGL release. Development and packaging were done on a Windows PC.

Creatively, the game combines spacecraft design with a playable flight campaign: the player moves from the hangar to launch, navigation, descent, and surface exploration rather than only reading about those phases. It uses NASA lunar imagery and elevation data, alongside published planetary reference values, to inform parts of its presentation and scenarios. The spacecraft components and many performance values are fictional game hardware, and the flight model is deliberately simplified for learning and play.

Key design considerations included making the first mission understandable, providing different difficulty levels, giving clear feedback on engineering tradeoffs, keeping the browser build practical to distribute, and distinguishing real reference data from fictional simulation values. The wider project also includes a crew-oriented expedition mode for supported builds; the itch.io WebGL build is primarily a solo experience. Some visual effects may be simplified in this browser build, and the flight simulation should be treated as an educational approximation rather than operationally accurate aerospace software.
